title: 瑞鹤仙·郊原初过雨
title_en: To the Tune Rui He Xian: Rain Has Just Passed Over the Fields
author: 袁去华

text_note.zh: 语料库“沈沈”是“沉沉”的旧写法，这里作“沉沉”。第六句有的本子作“遥山媚妩”，意思差不多，这里照语料库作“遥山眉妩”。
text_note.en: The corpus writes chén chén in an old character form; it is written here in the usual modern form. In line six some editions use a different character for méi (charming instead of eyebrows); the meaning is about the same, and this text follows the corpus.

readings.zh: 这里按“仍然、又”的意思读 hái。一说是“回去”的意思，读 huán。
readings.en: Read hái here, meaning "still, again". Another view takes it as "going back", read huán.

readings.zh: 这里是“再一次”的意思，读 chóng。
readings.en: Here it means "again", so it is read chóng.

readings.zh: 读 fǒu。在古代的读音里，它和“雨、舞、故”这些字押韵。
readings.en: Read fǒu. In old pronunciation it rhymed with yǔ, wǔ and gù.

glosses.en: jiāo yuán: open fields outside the town.

glosses.zh: 风定犹舞：风已经停了，叶子还在空中飘舞。
glosses.en: fēng dìng yóu wǔ: the wind has stopped, but the leaves are still dancing in the air.

glosses.zh: 浅黛：淡淡的青黑色。黛是古代女子画眉用的颜料，这里形容远山的颜色。
glosses.en: qiǎn dài: a light blue-black. Dài was the dark paint women once used on their eyebrows; here it is the colour of the far hills.

glosses.zh: 眉妩：眉毛画得妩媚好看。这里说远山像美人的眉毛。
glosses.en: méi wǔ: eyebrows lovely and charming. The far hills look like a beauty's eyebrows.
yán huā: flowers growing by the rocks.
rú gù: the same as before.

glosses.zh: 邮亭：古代路边供送信人和旅客歇脚的小屋。
glosses.en: yóu tíng: a small roadside house where messengers and travellers rested in old times.

glosses.zh: 旧曾题处：以前在墙上题过诗的地方。
glosses.en: jiù céng tí chù: the place where he once wrote a poem on the wall.

glosses.zh: 收香：晋朝贾充的女儿贾午爱上了韩寿，偷了家里珍贵的奇香送给他。这里借指男女相爱，互赠信物。
glosses.en: shōu xiāng: keeping the perfume. In the Jin dynasty a girl named Jia Wu loved a young man, Han Shou, and secretly gave him a rare perfume from her home. It stands for lovers giving each other keepsakes.

glosses.zh: 藏镜：南朝陈的乐昌公主和丈夫分别时，把一面镜子分成两半，各藏一半，后来凭它重逢。这里借指盼望重聚。
glosses.en: cáng jìng: hiding the mirror. A princess of the Chen dynasty and her husband broke a mirror in two when they parted, each keeping half, and later found each other by it. It stands for hoping to meet again.

glosses.zh: 人面桃花：唐代崔护的诗“人面不知何处去，桃花依旧笑春风”，说重来时，桃花还在，心爱的人却不见了。
glosses.en: rén miàn táo huā: from a Tang poem by Cui Hu. When he came back, the peach blossoms were still there, but the face he loved was gone.

translation.zh: 城外的原野上，雨刚刚下过。
translation.en: Rain has just passed over the fields outside the town.

translation.zh: 只见枯叶乱糟糟的，
translation.en: I see dead leaves lying everywhere,

translation.zh: 风停了，还在空中飞舞。
translation.en: and though the wind has stopped, some are still dancing.

translation.zh: 夕阳挂在深深的树林上。
translation.en: The setting sun hangs over the deep woods,

translation.zh: 映照着远山，山色一浓一淡，像带着愁意的眉黛，
translation.en: lighting the far hills, dark and pale like eyebrows painted with sorrow,

translation.zh: 远山就像美人妩媚的眉毛。
translation.en: the distant hills as lovely as a beauty's brows.

translation.zh: 这是我来时走过的老路，
translation.en: This is the old road I came by.

translation.zh: 山岩边的花还半开着，黄得娇嫩。
translation.en: By the rocks, the flowers are still half open, a tender yellow.

translation.zh: 到了今天，只有溪边的流水，
translation.en: Now only the water in the stream

translation.zh: 见到我还和从前一样。
translation.en: greets me just as it did before.

translation.zh: 我说不出话来。
translation.en: I have no words.

translation.zh: 路边的小驿亭又深又静，
translation.en: The little roadside rest house is deep and quiet.

translation.zh: 我下了马，还要去寻找
translation.en: I get off my horse and search again

translation.zh: 从前在墙上题诗的地方。
translation.en: for the place where I once wrote a poem on the wall.

translation.zh: 我这走累了的旅人，百无聊赖。
translation.en: I am a weary traveller, with nothing to cheer me.

translation.zh: 为离别的遗憾伤心，
translation.en: The pain of parting hurts me,

translation.zh: 这是最愁苦的事。
translation.en: and it is the bitterest sorrow of all.

translation.zh: 即使我们像古人一样留着信物，盼着重逢，
translation.en: Even if we keep our tokens like lovers of old and hope to meet again,

translation.zh: 将来我再来这里，
translation.en: when I come back here someday,

translation.zh: 那像桃花一样美的人还会在吗？
translation.en: will the face like peach blossom still be here?

translation.zh: 我想念那深深静静的小阁楼和幽暗的窗子，
translation.en: I think of the deep, quiet little room and its shaded window,

translation.zh: 有时会在梦里回到那里。
translation.en: and sometimes I go back there in my dreams.

background.zh: 这首词写作者重新走过从前走过的路，想起当年在这里遇到、后来分别的心上人。秋雨刚过，叶子枯落，他找到旧时题诗的地方，却见不到那个人了。词里写的是哪一年、哪个地方、思念的是谁，都没有留下记载，只能从词里去体会他的心情。
background.en: In this lyric the poet travels again along a road he once took. He remembers someone he loved, whom he met here and later had to leave. The autumn rain has just passed and the leaves are falling. He finds the place where he once wrote a poem on the wall, but she is nowhere to be seen. No record says which year, which place, or who she was; we can only feel his mood through the words.

author_note.zh: 袁去华，字宣卿，奉新（今属江西）人，生卒年不详。宋高宗绍兴十五年（1145）考中进士，做过善化、石首等地的知县，就是一个县的长官。他的词多写羁旅（在外漂泊）的愁苦和离别的思念，语言清新自然。
author_note.en: Yuan Quhua, also called Xuanqing, came from Fengxin in today's Jiangxi. His dates of birth and death are unknown. He passed the highest imperial exam in 1145 and served as head of counties such as Shanhua and Shishou. His lyrics often tell of the hardship of travelling far from home and the longing of parting, in fresh, natural words.

appreciation.zh: 这首词像一次“故地重游”。上阕先画风景：雨后的原野，枯叶在风停后还在飘，夕阳挂在树上，远山一深一浅，像美人画的眉。他走在来时的老路上，花还半开着，可是一切都变了，只有溪水像老朋友一样，见到他还是老样子。下阕他下马去找当年题诗的墙，心里又累又苦。他用了几个爱情故事：偷香、破镜、人面桃花，问自己：就算还留着信物，将来再来，她还会在吗？他不敢回答，只说有时会在梦里回到那间小阁楼。景物不变，人却不见了，这种“物是人非”的伤感最打动人。
appreciation.en: This lyric is like a visit to an old place. The first stanza paints the scene: fields after rain, dead leaves still floating after the wind has stopped, the sun hanging in the trees, and far hills dark and pale like a beauty's painted brows. He walks the road he once came by. The flowers are still half open, but everything has changed. Only the stream, like an old friend, greets him the same as ever. In the second stanza he gets off his horse to find the wall where he once wrote a poem, tired and sad. He thinks of old love stories: the stolen perfume, the broken mirror, the face among the peach blossoms. He asks himself: even if we kept our tokens, when I come again, will she still be here? He dares not answer, and only says that sometimes he goes back to that little room in his dreams. The places stay the same but the person is gone, and that feeling touches readers most.
